title: Product Video and Photo Glossary | AIVideosUGC
description: Plain-English definitions for the product photo, video, advertising, and ecommerce terms used across AIVideosUGC and links to the pages where each term matters.
h1: AIVideosUGC Glossary: Terms for Product Photos and Videos
lead: A short ecommerce glossary of product video terms and product photo terms. Open an entry when the word is new, then go to the page that uses it.

entries.definition: Credits are what each job spends. A product photo is 24 credits. A video is 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, and 120 for 30. The cost is on screen before you confirm, and a failed job returns its credits.

Aspect ratio is how wide a frame is compared with its height. A video can be 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4. Product photos are square. Pick the frame of the place you will post, then check the edges after you download.
Duration is how long a clip runs. You can choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. One action can stay short. An unboxing or a before-and-after needs time for both parts.

A white-background photo places the product on a plain, even white field with no extra props. Sellers use it for a marketplace main image. Start from a complete, in-focus product photo, then check that marketplace's current image rules before you publish.

A packshot is a clean product photograph where the item stands alone, so a shopper can judge its shape and finish. It is not a lifestyle scene with props or a person. The Every Angle template makes matching square views of the front, back, top, or base from a photo of each real side.

UGC means user-generated content. Here, a UGC-style ad uses a casual handheld look. An AI actor can speak a script, with captions and music on the clip. The person is generated, so it is not a real customer's review. Follow each platform's disclosure rules.

B-roll is supporting footage of a product, a hand, a detail, or an everyday action, rather than only a presenter facing the camera. That footage can sit under an AI voice, captions, and a music track.

Spark Ads are TikTok ads that promote an existing post. You can publish a clip to TikTok from the project, with an AI voice, captions, and music. Targeting, budget, and a Spark authorization still happen in TikTok Ads Manager. Do not present the actor as a customer.

Retargeting is advertising to people who already visited your shop, such as product viewers or cart users. AIVideosUGC can make the visual for that second look. It cannot see shopper history or pick the audience. Set visitors, exclusions, the offer, budget, and frequency in your ad platform.

A safe zone is the part of a social frame that stays visible after the platform covers the edges with buttons, captions, or profile controls. Final text is yours to add. Keep the product and any later text off the lower and right edges, then preview inside each ad manager.

A feed ad is a paid image or video in a scrolling social feed. The feed tools make a clear product scene, often square, with room for your message. A clip can already include captions, a voice, and music. Type the exact price yourself.

Ads Manager is the screen where an ad account sets audience, budget, placement, and schedule. You can publish the file to TikTok or Meta from AIVideosUGC, or download it. Type the price so it matches the live offer.

A product demo is a short clip of one useful action, such as a kettle pouring or a lid closing. Describe that single action and upload a photo that shows the moving part. Then compare the result with the real product.

An unboxing video follows the moment a package opens and the product comes out. The box, tissue, insert, and reveal order come from your description. The product photo anchors the item. Music can come from the library. Type the offer so it matches the live price.

Before-and-after shows the starting state, then the change the product makes. It fits a visible change, such as an organized drawer. Describe both halves. Do not claim a medical, body, or performance result unless the real product supports it.

A lifestyle photo places the product in an everyday setting so a shopper can picture owning it. A mug can sit beside a book. The scene is built from your product photo and your description. Compare the output with the real item before you use it.

An on-model photo shows clothing, jewelry, a bag, or another wearable on a generated model, so shoppers can see drape and scale. The tool does not supply measurements or confirm fit. Keep your size chart with the image.

A flat lay is a top-down arrangement of a product and a few props on a surface. Upload a photo of the full product, then describe the surface and the layout. Check that every item in the frame is something you actually sell.
A swatch is a small sample of color or finish shown beside the product, so a shopper can judge the shade. Generate it from your product photos, then add the shade name and the price yourself.
A variant is one purchasable option, such as a color, size, finish, or capacity. Upload a source photo for each option, then assign the downloaded files to the right option in Shopify or Amazon.

A carousel is several cards in one social ad, so people can swipe through products, angles, or variants. AIVideosUGC makes each image or clip. You set the order and add the text and destination in your ad account.

A CTA, or call to action, is the short line that tells someone what to do next, such as shop or view the product. Put that line in the script or the captions. Type the date and the price so they match the live offer.

AI-generated content is an image or video an AI model creates or changes, rather than a frame captured only by a camera. Check every result against the real item. Do not present a generated person as a customer. Follow the disclosure rules of the platform where you publish.
A caption is timed text on a video, or the written line of a social post. Clips can include captions. Edit them in the built-in editor so the price, date, and code match the live offer.
Spoken narration is a voice track on a video. An AI actor speaks the line you write, in the language you choose. That speech is not a customer review. You can change the voice in the editor.

A template is a ready-made direction for one product job, such as a white background, an unboxing, or a short demo. Upload the product photo, follow the notes on that template, and run another job when you want a different direction.

A marketplace listing is the product page you keep on a selling platform such as Amazon or Etsy. That platform sets the image slots and video rules. Download the files and check the current seller rules before you upload them.

DTC means direct-to-consumer. The brand sells through its own online store, not only through a marketplace. Sellers use the photos and short clips on that store, in a social feed, in email, and in ads.

An AI actor is a generated presenter who can hold, wear, or talk about a product. You pick one from the actor library or describe the look. The person is not a customer and does not replace a size chart.
An AI script is a spoken line drafted from the product and the buyer you describe. You can edit every sentence before the actor says it. The line should only claim what the real item does.
An AI voice is the spoken track an actor uses for the line you write. You choose the language by writing the line in it. The voice is generated. It is not a recording of a customer.

The API lets your own tools start a product photo or a video job. The credit cost matches the same job in the project. A failed job returns its credits. A product photo is 24 credits. A video is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds.

A batch is several jobs from one product photo, each with its own scene, frame, or opening line. Every job shows its credit cost before it starts. Download the versions you want, or publish a finished file to TikTok or Meta.
The built-in editor changes a finished file without a second app. You can revise the spoken line, the captions, the voice, the music, and the presenter, then export again.

Link to video starts a clip from a public product page. The page's main image and product name are the reference. Prices and reviews on the page are not copied in. You still pick the frame and the length.
The music library is a set of tracks you can put under a product clip. Swap the track in the editor. You still write the spoken line, and you are responsible for what that line claims.
One-click publish sends a finished photo or video to TikTok or Meta from the project. You can download the file instead. Audience, budget, placement, and schedule still live in the ad account.
